messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] SQLite Database reverting to earlier version (lost information)
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] SQLite Database reverting to earlier version (lost information)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jesse,
Presuming you haven't redeployed your application, the data is probably still there. We encourage everyone to think of storage on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> as transient so in an ideal world you would have a way of backing up the data to a location you control and pulling it down on application start.
When an application is deployed we actually place it on multiple servers for the sake of redundancy. When an application is not receiving any traffic it will "go to sleep" and the next time it is requested it may or may not start on the same server it was started on the last time.  You might be able to find your data by stopping the instance (in the application tab in the dashboard) and restarting it.   Hopefully it won't take more than 3 tries for you to find the instance that has the up to date data.

We are looking at how we can make the pattern for persistent storage a little easier for everyone.

Hope this helps.
Tareef

I'm not sure what to with this.  Thanks for any help.

messages.subject: Difficulty connecting to AWS redshift database using shinyapps
messages.subject_clean: Difficulty connecting to AWS redshift database using shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
Hello.  I have data saved on a AWS redshift server that would like to load from my deployed shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app.  On my local machine I have used RODBC library to establish a ODBC connection sing driver DSN setup using the redshift driver (see link http://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/install-odbc-driver-windows.html).  Then I just used "odbcConnect" RODBC function to establish the connection in my R session.  Does anyone know I can do this with Shiny and Shinyapps, or have any other suggestions on how to establish a connection to the database?

I also found some other discussions on how I might do this, but I could not understand Tareef Kawaf response.  He also mentioned that they are writing an article about this, and was wondering if anyone knew whether they had yet?
https://support.rstudio.com/hc/communities/public/questions/203051837-How-to-Connect-to-External-Database-AWS-?locale=en-us

Thanks in advance for any comments/suggestions!

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chad

I am trying to setup a mysql connection to my shinyapp using Amazon's RDS servers. Everything works locally as I have whitelisted my office IP address to connect to the database, however it does not work when deployed. I tried whitelisting the IP addresses you listed in hopes that my app would connect once live, but alas no luck.

I guess my question is, where did you find the IP addresses for the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers? I don't know if they have changed or expanded since you posted back in February. How would I go about finding that information?

Thank you for your help
Scott Shepard

On Monday, February 2, 2015 at 7:57:42 AM UTC-6, Chad Barraford wrote:
>
> Hello,
> Can you configure your mysql server to have port 3306 open to the following IP addresses? These are the addresses your app may be running from. That would allow you to connect from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers to your remote MySQL server.
> 54.204.37.78
>
> 54.204.29.251
>
> 54.204.36.75
>
> 54.204.34.9
>
> If you can’t do that, port forwarding could work. That will allow you to connect to your mysql server as if its running locally (of course it actually wouldn’t be). Something like
> ssh -nNTL 3306:localhost:3306 username@hostname
> That command won’t exit (unless the connection is broken), so you’ll prob need to run it as a background process (which you can do in R or add an ampersand (&) to the end of the ssh command.
>
> Hope that helps
> ​
>
> On Sun, Feb 1, 2015 at 10:41 AM, Phill Clarke <phill...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > I'm struggling to connect to remote MySQL database, via an SSH tunnel and was hoping someone on here may have an idea to assist.
> >
> > The scenario is that my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app needs to retrieve data from a MySQL database, located on a remote server. This part is simple enough using the RMySQL library, something like this:
> >
> > library("RMySQL")
> >
> > con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host="hostname", user="username", pwd="password", dbname="databasename", port=3306)
> >
> > sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM databasename.tablename", sep="")
> >
> > results <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
> >
> > dbDisconnect(con)
> >
> > The problem is that the database does not accept remote connections.
> >
> > If I was to tackle this problem "manually", I'd ssh into the machine and execute the SQL query on localhost. Obviously that won't work in this case.
> >
> > I've been trying to setup an auto-closing ssh tunnel with something like this:
> >
> > system(paste("sshpass -p 'passwordhere' ssh -f -L 22:127.0.0.1:3306 <http://127.0.0.1:3306> username@hostname sleep 10"))
> >
> > I'm basically trying to bind the local port 22 to the remote port 3306. If there's no activity, the ssh tunnel closes in 10 seconds.
> >
> > I know I could use public/private keys rather than a password, and will probably do so for the production code, but I was just testing with an actual password to establish the connection.
> >
> > I've been using ps aux | grep sshd to check the tunnel is created and then after 10 seconds of non-activity closes. This bit seems to work fine.
> >
> > However, I'm still somewhat stuck when trying to execute my local MySQL query. The error is:
> >
> > Error in .local(drv, ...) :
> >   Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'hostname' (111)
> >
> > Which is the same error I see without the ssh tunnel, so clearly the query is not using the tunnel and this is where I am stuck. I'm guessing the local port binding might be wrong, but not really sure how to fix it.
> >
> > If someone can provide a solution, obviously I'd like it to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the local port binding would need to be one that is available on the service.
> >
> > I guess there are other convoluted options, like running the SQL query on the same machine as the database, saving results as a CSV and then making that CSV available to my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app. This is not ideal, because I'd like to write data back to the database too, and this ust seems like an intermediate step which is not really optimum.
> >

You will then need to run:

shinyapps:::detectLocale.Windows(FALSE)

And then redeploy your application.

Does someone know how to fix it ?

Stéfane

messages.body_plain:
Of course.

I was not responsible for setting up the mysql server I connected to, but amazon has a great resource here

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_GettingStarted.CreatingConnecting.MySQL.html

To ensure that my shiny app could always connect to our servers, I added RStudio's EC2 Security Group to the database I was connecting to.

1. Log into your Amazon AWS console
2. Click on the RDS Dashboard under the Database section
3. Navigate to the Security Groups tab
4. Select the database you want to allow access to
5. At the very bottom there is a dropdown for Connection Type, select EC2 Security Group
6. Select Another Account
7. Enter the account ID and Security Group name for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>:

      AWS Account ID: 954555569365
      EC2 Security Group Name: production-agents

8. Authorize!

And you're done. The shinyapps servers have access to your MySQL database without making system calls or setting up an ssh tunnel.

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am trying to deploy our Shiny app to ShinyApps.io._ One of the dependencies of the app is a GitHub project which is a private repo belonging to our organization. Since the repo belongs to the organization and not a user it seems we might have to do things slightly differently than what is recommended in the guide: https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/204536558-Enabling-use-of-private-packages-on-github-com

When I try to install the package locally, as expected it doesn't work without authenticating:
> install_github("mycompany/my-package", subdir="packagex")
Downloading github repo prismfp/prismfp-package@master
Error in download(dest, src, auth) : client error: (404) Not Found

If I try to authenticate using a password (using my personal GH account), it still fails:
> install_github("mycompany/my-package", auth_user="myname", password="trustno1", subdir="packagex")
Downloading github repo prismfp/prismfp-package@master
Error in download(dest, src, auth) : client error: (404) Not Found

I generated an authentication token for my personal account on GitHub, and used this to install instead of the password:

> install_github("mycompany/my-package", subdir="packagex", auth_token="15efaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa414a")
Downloading github repo mycompany/prismfp-package@master
Installing packagex
...

This seemed to work fine. I had the line library("packagex") in my code, and I hoped for the package to be automatically installed on deploy. However I got the error message:

> shinyapps::deployApp('.')
Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading application bundle...DONE
Deploying application: 41756...
Waiting for task: 32072061
  building: Parsing manifest
  building: Building image: 179292
  building: Building package: packagex
################################## Begin Log ##################################
################################### End Log ###################################
Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 32072062 failed: Error building image: Error fetching packagex (0.23.0) source. Error accessing GitHub repository mycompany/my-package. HTTP 404: Not Found

I added my personal GitHub account 'myname' to 'GitHub authentication' in the ShinyApps.io dashboard, and ticked 'Private Repository Access'. However I still saw the same message as above when trying to deploy.

I think that possibly shinyapps::deployApp() makes some assumption when installing packages that the first part of the repo identifier (here the organization name 'mycompany') is the same as the user name (here 'myname') and that the installation fails if this is not the case. Am I doing something else wrong or can this problem be fixed or worked around?

Thanks in advance for your help,
Jack Grahl

Hi

I am actually loading the packages from a private organization.

First, make sure you install the packages with the auth token.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a ggvis plot that is displayed properly in R but that is scaled in the app hosted at shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> in a way that one has to drag the lower right corner to see all the data points along the x axis. Could you please indicated what might be the issue?

Code for the plot (includes a sample data frame):

plotdfN0<-data.frame(cbind(c(1,1,2,2,3,3),c(1,2,1,2,1,2)))
colnames(plotdfN0)<-c("treats","N0")

se <- function(x) sqrt(var(x,na.rm=TRUE)/length(x))

plotdf<- plotdfN0 %>% group_by(treats) %>% summarise(N0mean=mean(N0),N0sd=sd(N0),N0se=se(N0))
plotdf$N0sd[which(is.na <http://is.na>(plotdf$N0sd))]<-0
plotdf$N0se[which(is.na <http://is.na>(plotdf$N0se))]<-0
plotdf<-rbind(mutate(plotdf,N0sdbar=N0mean-N0sd,N0sebar=N0mean-N0se),
              mutate(plotdf,N0sdbar=N0mean+N0sd,N0sebar=N0mean+N0se))
plotdf<- plotdf %>% select(-N0sd,-N0se) %>% arrange(treats)
plotdf<- left_join(plotdf,plotdfN0)

upperlimit<-round(max(plotdfN0$N0),0)

plotdf %>% ggvis(opacity:=1) %>%
  layer_points(x=~treats,y=~N0mean,shape:="diamond",size:=100) %>%
  group_by(treats) %>%
  layer_paths(x=~treats,y=~N0sdbar,strokeWidth:=3,stroke:="black") %>%
  layer_paths(x=~treats,y=~N0sebar,strokeWidth:=3) %>%
  layer_points(x=~treats,y=~N0,fill:="red",opacity:=1) %>%
  scale_numeric("y", domain = input_slider(min=0,max=upperlimit,value=c(0,upperlimit),label="Set Y-axis range:")) %>%
  add_axis("y",grid=F,title="Hill's N0",title_offset=50,
           properties=axis_props(labels=list(fontSize=14,align="right"),title=list(fontSize=16))
  ) %>%
  add_axis("x",grid=F,title="",properties=axis_props(labels=list(fontSize=14,angle=270,align="right")))

The plot is embedded within the observe function in the app.

Thanks in advance!

Cheers,
Bogdan

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: deployApp failure with private/organization GitHub repo as dependency
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Re: deployApp failure with private/organization GitHub repo as dependency
messages.body_plain:
Juan is correct. Within an GitHub organization's settings page, there is a setting for "3rd party access". 3rd party access needs to be enabled with no restrictions to allow the organization's member's authorized GiHub applications (e.g shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>) to access not only the users's repositories, but the organization's content as well.

-Andy

On Sat, May 9, 2015 at 11:11 AM, Juan <jpmar...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi
>
>
> I am actually loading the packages from a private organization.
>
> First, make sure you install the packages with the auth token.
> install_github("mycompany/my-package", subdir="packagex", auth_token="15efaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa414a")
>
> Second,
> Make sure to tick the organization access when you authorize github on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. Make sure the Check mark is GREEN for the desired organization. I was having the same issue until I realized that the organization chek mark was not green.
>
> That should do it, cheers
>
>
>
>
>
>
>
> On Friday, May 8, 2015 at 10:04:21 AM UTC-5, ja...@prismfp.com wrote:
> > Hi there,
> >
> > I am trying to deploy our Shiny app to ShinyApps.io._ One of the dependencies of the app is a GitHub project which is a private repo belonging to our organization. Since the repo belongs to the organization and not a user it seems we might have to do things slightly differently than what is recommended in the guide: https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/204536558-Enabling-use-of-private-packages-on-github-com
> >
> > When I try to install the package locally, as expected it doesn't work without authenticating:
> > > install_github("mycompany/my-package", subdir="packagex")
> > Downloading github repo prismfp/prismfp-package@master
> > Error in download(dest, src, auth) : client error: (404) Not Found
> >
> > If I try to authenticate using a password (using my personal GH account), it still fails:
> > > install_github("mycompany/my-package", auth_user="myname", password="trustno1", subdir="packagex")
> > Downloading github repo prismfp/prismfp-package@master
> > Error in download(dest, src, auth) : client error: (404) Not Found
> >
> > I generated an authentication token for my personal account on GitHub, and used this to install instead of the password:
> >
> > > install_github("mycompany/my-package", subdir="packagex", auth_token="15efaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa414a")
> > Downloading github repo mycompany/prismfp-package@master
> > Installing packagex
> > ...
> >
> > This seemed to work fine. I had the line library("packagex") in my code, and I hoped for the package to be automatically installed on deploy. However I got the error message:
> >
> > > shinyapps::deployApp('.')
> > Preparing to deploy application...DONE
> > Uploading application bundle...DONE
> > Deploying application: 41756...
> > Waiting for task: 32072061
> >   building: Parsing manifest
> >   building: Building image: 179292
> >   building: Building package: packagex
> > ################################## Begin Log ##################################
> > ################################### End Log ###################################
> > Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 32072062 failed: Error building image: Error fetching packagex (0.23.0) source. Error accessing GitHub repository mycompany/my-package. HTTP 404: Not Found
> >
> > I added my personal GitHub account 'myname' to 'GitHub authentication' in the ShinyApps.io dashboard, and ticked 'Private Repository Access'. However I still saw the same message as above when trying to deploy.
> >
> > I think that possibly shinyapps::deployApp() makes some assumption when installing packages that the first part of the repo identifier (here the organization name 'mycompany') is the same as the user name (here 'myname') and that the installation fails if this is not the case. Am I doing something else wrong or can this problem be fixed or worked around?
> >
> > Thanks in advance for your help,
> > Jack Grahl

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io hungarian encoding
messages.body_plain:
We've recently improved support for detecting and installing locales on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. Can you try upgrading to the latest version of the shinyapps package:

devtools::install_github('rstudio/shinyapps')

After then, can you run:

shinyapps:::detectLocale()

And let me know what the output is.

-Andy

messages.body_snippet:
I would make sure the source data is encoded as UTF-8 rather then attempting to convert it. If you are using RStudio, you can go to File -> Save with Encoding.

On Mon, May 11, 2015 at 3:19 PM, Ádám G

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io hungarian encoding
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] shinyapps.io hungarian encoding
messages.body_plain:
I save the source code to utf-8 encoding.
If I miss the textCorpus = tm_map(textCorpus, content_transformer(function(x) iconv(x, to="ISO-8859-2", sub='byte')), mc.cores=1) command, i get this error:
Error: no applicable method for 'meta' applied to an object of class "try-error"

I modified the source text to utf-8 encoding.

Any idea?
Thanks

http://adamgmoser.shinyapps.io/wordfreq-app
this is a word cloud and frequency app. now it shows the words, but the special characters are replaced with english alphabet letters.
e.g. in lit_er_balasi.txt:
miért -> miert
már -> mer
jön -> jfn

I found this artice about encodings: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/unicode.html

messages.subject: No support for 'subdir' where using GitHub
messages.subject_clean: No support for 'subdir' where using GitHub
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I have been trying to deploy our app to ShinyApps.io using a custom package which I have put as a private repo on Github.com._ My previous question at https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shinyapps-users/JRfN4UBcVQs explains the setup and a problem I had with the repository permissioning which has now been fixed.

It now seems that I can't use the 'subdir' argument to install_github and have SA.io correctly install my package. The package directory was originally in a subdirectory of the repo root.

> install_github("mycompany/mypackage", subdir="packagename", auth_token="15ef...414a")
Downloading github repo prismfp/mypackage@master
Installing packagename
...

* installing *source* package 'packagename' ...
...
* DONE (packagename)
> shinyapps::deployApp('.')
Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading application bundle...DONE
Deploying application: 41756...
Waiting for task: 32976894
  building: Parsing manifest
  building: Building image: 180996
  building: Fetching packages
  error: Building package: packagename
################################## Begin Log ##################################
################################### End Log ###################################
Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 32976895 failed: Error building image: Error fetching packagename (0.23.0) source. Package source does not appear to be a package

I then changed the github repository so that the files in the 'packagename' directory were moved to the root directory of the repository. I reran the above two commands, omitting the 'subdir=' from the install_github call. The app installed packages and deployed correctly.

I wanted to know - am I doing things incorrectly or is the subdir argument to install_github not currently supported? If not, is there any possibility that it could be in the future? I can live with the workaround above, but would much prefer not to have to use it.

Thanks very much,
Jack

messages.body_plain:
Jack,

The subdir parameter is supported (a change I made a few weeks back). By any chance do you have a mixed case repository?

I have seen some issues when there is case mismatch. For example:

If your repo name is 'MyPackage' running install_github('someuser/mypackage', subdir="derp") works when installing locally, but will fail to install on shinyapps. In this case you need to ensure you use the exact repository name: install_github('someuser/MyPackage', subdir="derp")

This is only an issue when using the subdir parameter (When not using a subdir, any casing on the repo name is fine).

-Andy

messages.subject: Updates to shinyapps.io (May 13, 2015)
messages.subject_clean: Updates to shinyapps.io (May 13, 2015)
messages.body_plain:
We are happy to announce the latest set of changes to the shinyapps.io <http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps> platform.  This release addresses some of the top requests we have heard. Please try them out and let us know what you think:

-       Increase application upload size – you can now include up to 1GB of data with your application bundles to use in your analyses.

-       Improved locale detection support – the updated shinyapps package can now detect and map your locale appropriately if your locale varies from the locale of shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>  (requires shinyapps package update)

-       Installing larger R packages – historically shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> couldn’t support installation of packages that exceeded 100MB; we have now increased the limit to 1GB. (This is primarily relevant to users of BioConductor packages)

-       Account Rename - did you pick a name for your account and wish you had selected a different one? You can now make that change in your account settings. (Note: old URLs will no longer work)

-       Account Transfer – If you created an account on behalf of your organization and now would like someone else to be the owner of the account, you can now transfer ownership of your account to them. (Note: You can’t get the account back unless the new owner transfers it to you)

-       Support for newer versions of R – you can now use R 3.1.3 and 3.2.0.

As always, we are looking for your feedback.  Please drop us a line and let us know how else we can improve shinyapps.io <http://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps>.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Remote MySQL database with SSH Tunnel
messages.body_plain:
Tim,

I may be wrong, but I have tried to do this with a VPC, and I have concluded that the only way is to allow access from the individual IP addresses mentioned in Chad Barraford's post above from 2 Feb.

If you find out how to get it to work using ShinyApps.io's security group, then I would be pleased to hear about it. However it seems that in any case you would have to be in the same AWS geographic zone as the ShinyApps servers for this to work. IP addresses work anywhere.

Jack

On Friday, 8 May 2015 00:49:47 UTC+1, Tim Beveridge wrote:
> Thanks Phil. That's a great guide. I'm new to the Amazon services and have set up a free RDS MySQL server. It exists inside a VPC and hence you can only use VPC security groups to control access.
>
> I'm wondering if you have any tips on setting the security in that environment so shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> can access it :-)
>
> Cheers,
>
> Tim
>
> On Thursday, May 7, 2015 at 7:27:08 AM UTC+10, Scott Shepard wrote:
> > Of course.
> >
> > I was not responsible for setting up the mysql server I connected to, but amazon has a great resource here
> >
> > https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_GettingStarted.CreatingConnecting.MySQL.html
> >
> > To ensure that my shiny app could always connect to our servers, I added RStudio's EC2 Security Group to the database I was connecting to.
> >
> > 1. Log into your Amazon AWS console
> > 2. Click on the RDS Dashboard under the Database section
> > 3. Navigate to the Security Groups tab
> > 4. Select the database you want to allow access to
> > 5. At the very bottom there is a dropdown for Connection Type, select EC2 Security Group
> > 6. Select Another Account
> > 7. Enter the account ID and Security Group name for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>:
> >       AWS Account ID: 954555569365
> >       EC2 Security Group Name: production-agents
> > 8. Authorize!
> >
> > And you're done. The shinyapps servers have access to your MySQL database without making system calls or setting up an ssh tunnel.
> >
> > On Tuesday, May 5, 2015 at 12:54:29 PM UTC-5, Paolo Cavatore wrote:
> > > A Step-by-Step guide would be appreciated if possible...hopefully using Amazon RDS
> > >
> > > On Monday, 4 May 2015 20:30:34 UTC+2, Scott Shepard wrote:
> > > > Thank you that worked wonderfully.
> > > >
> > > > On Monday, May 4, 2015 at 12:23:17 PM UTC-5, Chad Barraford wrote:
> > > > > Hi Scott,
> > > > > Theres a slight better way of doing this. In your security group for your RDS instance, allow traffic from the following. This should give our servers access to your RDS server, even as we provision/retire nodes.
> > > > >
> > > > > AWS Account ID: 954555569365
> > > > > EC2 Security Group Name: production-agents
> > > > >
> > > > > On Mon, May 4, 2015 at 11:54 AM, Scott Shepard <sco...@esparklearning.com> wrote:
> > > > > > Hi Chad
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I am trying to setup a mysql connection to my shinyapp using Amazon's RDS servers. Everything works locally as I have whitelisted my office IP address to connect to the database, however it does not work when deployed. I tried whitelisting the IP addresses you listed in hopes that my app would connect once live, but alas no luck.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I guess my question is, where did you find the IP addresses for the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers? I don't know if they have changed or expanded since you posted back in February. How would I go about finding that information?
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Thank you for your help
> > > > > > Scott Shepard
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Monday, February 2, 2015 at 7:57:42 AM UTC-6, Chad Barraford wrote:
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Hello,
> > > > > > > Can you configure your mysql server to have port 3306 open to the following IP addresses? These are the addresses your app may be running from. That would allow you to connect from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers to your remote MySQL server.
> > > > > > > 54.204.37.78
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 54.204.29.251
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 54.204.36.75
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 54.204.34.9
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > If you can’t do that, port forwarding could work. That will allow you to connect to your mysql server as if its running locally (of course it actually wouldn’t be). Something like
> > > > > > > ssh -nNTL 3306:localhost:3306 username@hostname
> > > > > > > That command won’t exit (unless the connection is broken), so you’ll prob need to run it as a background process (which you can do in R or add an ampersand (&) to the end of the ssh command.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Hope that helps
> > > > > > > ​
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On Sun, Feb 1, 2015 at 10:41 AM, Phill Clarke <phill...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > I'm struggling to connect to remote MySQL database, via an SSH tunnel and was hoping someone on here may have an idea to assist.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > The scenario is that my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app needs to retrieve data from a MySQL database, located on a remote server. This part is simple enough using the RMySQL library, something like this:
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > library("RMySQL")
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host="hostname", user="username", pwd="password", dbname="databasename", port=3306)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM databasename.tablename", sep="")
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > results <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > dbDisconnect(con)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > The problem is that the database does not accept remote connections.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > If I was to tackle this problem "manually", I'd ssh into the machine and execute the SQL query on localhost. Obviously that won't work in this case.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > I've been trying to setup an auto-closing ssh tunnel with something like this:
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > system(paste("sshpass -p 'passwordhere' ssh -f -L 22:127.0.0.1:3306 <http://127.0.0.1:3306> username@hostname sleep 10"))
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > I'm basically trying to bind the local port 22 to the remote port 3306. If there's no activity, the ssh tunnel closes in 10 seconds.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > I know I could use public/private keys rather than a password, and will probably do so for the production code, but I was just testing with an actual password to establish the connection.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > I've been using ps aux | grep sshd to check the tunnel is created and then after 10 seconds of non-activity closes. This bit seems to work fine.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > However, I'm still somewhat stuck when trying to execute my local MySQL query. The error is:
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Error in .local(drv, ...) :
> > > > > > > >   Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'hostname' (111)
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Which is the same error I see without the ssh tunnel, so clearly the query is not using the tunnel and this is where I am stuck. I'm guessing the local port binding might be wrong, but not really sure how to fix it.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > If someone can provide a solution, obviously I'd like it to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the local port binding would need to be one that is available on the service.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > I guess there are other convoluted options, like running the SQL query on the same machine as the database, saving results as a CSV and then making that CSV available to my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app. This is not ideal, because I'd like to write data back to the database too, and this ust seems like an intermediate step which is not really optimum.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >

Andy,

The name of our package doesn't have any upper case. I updated shinyApps and devtools locally to the most recent github versions in case that solved the problem but it didn't seem to.

I would be very happy if you have any further thoughts on this.

Thanks ia,
Jack

On Tuesday, 12 May 2015 14:45:14 UTC+1, Andy Kipp wrote:
> Jack,
>
> The subdir parameter is supported (a change I made a few weeks back). By any chance do you have a mixed case repository?
>
> I have seen some issues when there is case mismatch. For example:
>
> If your repo name is 'MyPackage' running install_github('someuser/mypackage', subdir="derp") works when installing locally, but will fail to install on shinyapps. In this case you need to ensure you use the exact repository name: install_github('someuser/MyPackage', subdir="derp")
>
> This is only an issue when using the subdir parameter (When not using a subdir, any casing on the repo name is fine).
>
> -Andy
>

> >
> > I have been trying to deploy our app to ShinyApps.io using a custom package which I have put as a private repo on Github.com._ My previous question at https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shinyapps-users/JRfN4UBcVQs explains the setup and a problem I had with the repository permissioning which has now been fixed.
> >
> > It now seems that I can't use the 'subdir' argument to install_github and have SA.io correctly install my package. The package directory was originally in a subdirectory of the repo root.
> >
> > > install_github("mycompany/mypackage", subdir="packagename", auth_token="15ef...414a")
> > Downloading github repo prismfp/mypackage@master
> > Installing packagename
> > ...
> >
> > * installing *source* package 'packagename' ...
> > ...
> > * DONE (packagename)
> > > shinyapps::deployApp('.')
> > Preparing to deploy application...DONE
> > Uploading application bundle...DONE
> > Deploying application: 41756...
> > Waiting for task: 32976894
> >   building: Parsing manifest
> >   building: Building image: 180996
> >   building: Fetching packages
> >   error: Building package: packagename
> > ################################## Begin Log ##################################
> > ################################### End Log ###################################
> > Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 32976895 failed: Error building image: Error fetching packagename (0.23.0) source. Package source does not appear to be a package
> >
> > I then changed the github repository so that the files in the 'packagename' directory were moved to the root directory of the repository. I reran the above two commands, omitting the 'subdir=' from the install_github call. The app installed packages and deployed correctly.
> >
> > I wanted to know - am I doing things incorrectly or is the subdir argument to install_github not currently supported? If not, is there any possibility that it could be in the future? I can live with the workaround above, but would much prefer not to have to use it.
> >
> > Thanks very much,

Thank you in advance.

messages.body_plain:
Sorry about that. I think this is due to a recent change I made in
shiny: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/823 but I cannot imagine
how the error you mentioned could occur (the error should be from
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/808d7aab3f6/R/update-input.R#L453
I think NULL was passed to fromJSON() then introduced the error).

The selectize input (server = TRUE) in shiny 0.12 does not really load
all the options at once: it loads the first n options specified in the
option maxOptions initially. The default value of maxOptions is 1000.
You can reduce this number via the `options` argument, e.g.

library(shiny)
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    selectizeInput('foo', 'Foo', choices = NULL, options = list(maxOptions = 5))
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    updateSelectizeInput(session, 'foo', choices = letters, server = TRUE)
  }
)

If you can provide a minimal example to reproduce your problem, I can
certainly fix it. Thanks a lot!

Regards,
Yihui
--

You should assume that the files will be lost since the files that are being uploaded will be written to temporary storage (unless you do something like put them in a more permanent data store, or we provide persistent storage as part of the platform).  That temporary storage essentially goes away when the application goes to sleep for lack of usage, and comes back clean when it starts up again.

messages.body_plain:
You only need to have the library() call in your code.  shinyapps will pick up which versions of the packages you are using and re-install them on the server.  That does mean that the packages you are using have to be on CRAN, Github (private or public) or BioConductor.
For private packages, you would want to put it in on a private repo on Github.

Hope this helps.
-Tareef

On Saturday, May 16, 2015 at 1:06:04 AM UTC+10, ja...@prismfp.com wrote:
> Tim,
>
> I may be wrong, but I have tried to do this with a VPC, and I have concluded that the only way is to allow access from the individual IP addresses mentioned in Chad Barraford's post above from 2 Feb.
>
> If you find out how to get it to work using ShinyApps.io's security group, then I would be pleased to hear about it. However it seems that in any case you would have to be in the same AWS geographic zone as the ShinyApps servers for this to work. IP addresses work anywhere.
>
> Jack
>
> On Friday, 8 May 2015 00:49:47 UTC+1, Tim Beveridge wrote:
> > Thanks Phil. That's a great guide. I'm new to the Amazon services and have set up a free RDS MySQL server. It exists inside a VPC and hence you can only use VPC security groups to control access.
> >
> > I'm wondering if you have any tips on setting the security in that environment so shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> can access it :-)
> >
> > Cheers,
> >
> > Tim
> >
> > On Thursday, May 7, 2015 at 7:27:08 AM UTC+10, Scott Shepard wrote:
> > > Of course.
> > >
> > > I was not responsible for setting up the mysql server I connected to, but amazon has a great resource here
> > >
> > > https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_GettingStarted.CreatingConnecting.MySQL.html
> > >
> > > To ensure that my shiny app could always connect to our servers, I added RStudio's EC2 Security Group to the database I was connecting to.
> > >
> > > 1. Log into your Amazon AWS console
> > > 2. Click on the RDS Dashboard under the Database section
> > > 3. Navigate to the Security Groups tab
> > > 4. Select the database you want to allow access to
> > > 5. At the very bottom there is a dropdown for Connection Type, select EC2 Security Group
> > > 6. Select Another Account
> > > 7. Enter the account ID and Security Group name for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>:
> > >       AWS Account ID: 954555569365
> > >       EC2 Security Group Name: production-agents
> > > 8. Authorize!
> > >
> > > And you're done. The shinyapps servers have access to your MySQL database without making system calls or setting up an ssh tunnel.
> > >
> > > On Tuesday, May 5, 2015 at 12:54:29 PM UTC-5, Paolo Cavatore wrote:
> > > > A Step-by-Step guide would be appreciated if possible...hopefully using Amazon RDS
> > > >
> > > > On Monday, 4 May 2015 20:30:34 UTC+2, Scott Shepard wrote:
> > > > > Thank you that worked wonderfully.
> > > > >
> > > > > On Monday, May 4, 2015 at 12:23:17 PM UTC-5, Chad Barraford wrote:
> > > > > > Hi Scott,
> > > > > > Theres a slight better way of doing this. In your security group for your RDS instance, allow traffic from the following. This should give our servers access to your RDS server, even as we provision/retire nodes.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > AWS Account ID: 954555569365
> > > > > > EC2 Security Group Name: production-agents
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Mon, May 4, 2015 at 11:54 AM, Scott Shepard <sco...@esparklearning.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > Hi Chad
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > I am trying to setup a mysql connection to my shinyapp using Amazon's RDS servers. Everything works locally as I have whitelisted my office IP address to connect to the database, however it does not work when deployed. I tried whitelisting the IP addresses you listed in hopes that my app would connect once live, but alas no luck.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > I guess my question is, where did you find the IP addresses for the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers? I don't know if they have changed or expanded since you posted back in February. How would I go about finding that information?
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Thank you for your help
> > > > > > > Scott Shepard
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On Monday, February 2, 2015 at 7:57:42 AM UTC-6, Chad Barraford wrote:
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Hello,
> > > > > > > > Can you configure your mysql server to have port 3306 open to the following IP addresses? These are the addresses your app may be running from. That would allow you to connect from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers to your remote MySQL server.
> > > > > > > > 54.204.37.78
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > 54.204.29.251
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > 54.204.36.75
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > 54.204.34.9
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > If you can’t do that, port forwarding could work. That will allow you to connect to your mysql server as if its running locally (of course it actually wouldn’t be). Something like
> > > > > > > > ssh -nNTL 3306:localhost:3306 username@hostname
> > > > > > > > That command won’t exit (unless the connection is broken), so you’ll prob need to run it as a background process (which you can do in R or add an ampersand (&) to the end of the ssh command.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Hope that helps
> > > > > > > > ​
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On Sun, Feb 1, 2015 at 10:41 AM, Phill Clarke <phill...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > I'm struggling to connect to remote MySQL database, via an SSH tunnel and was hoping someone on here may have an idea to assist.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > The scenario is that my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app needs to retrieve data from a MySQL database, located on a remote server. This part is simple enough using the RMySQL library, something like this:
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > library("RMySQL")
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > con <- dbConnect(MySQL(), host="hostname", user="username", pwd="password", dbname="databasename", port=3306)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > sql1 <- paste("SELECT * FROM databasename.tablename", sep="")
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > results <- dbGetQuery(con, sql1)
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > dbDisconnect(con)
> > > > > > > > >

I am not 100% sure if this helps, but I know some people use security groups for this purpose as well.  From our FAQ.

You’ll need to add RStudio’s EC2 Security Group to the database:

1. Log into your Amazon AWS console
2. Click on the RDS Dashboard under the Database section
3. Navigate to the Security Groups tab
4. Select the database you want to allow access to
5. At the very bottom there is a dropdown for Connection Type, select EC2 Security Group
6. Select Another Account
7. Enter the account ID and Security Group name for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>:
AWS Account ID: 954555569365
EC2 Security Group Name: production-agents
8. Authorize!

messages.subject: using sendmailR package with Shiny
messages.subject_clean: using sendmailR package with Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Below is an MRE that works fine locally, but which fails on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> (except for the dummy gmail addresses).

Checking the logs, the mailer doesn't get a connection: "SMTP 421".

Is there a (security) reason this functionality fails on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and/or shinyServer?

library(shiny)
library(sendmailR)

ui <- shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
  actionButton("sendSignal", "Press 3x to Send"),
  textOutput("my_button"),
  textInput("subject", "Subject:", value="")
))

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

output$my_button <- renderText(input$sendSignal)

  ##Send an email after actionButton pressed a few times; use some input from UI
  observe({
    if(input$sendSignal == 3)
      sendmail(from = "<te...@gmail.com>",
               to = "<tes...@gmail.com <http://mail.com>>",
               subject = isolate(input$subject),
               msg = mime_part(mtcars),  ##
               control=list(smtpServer="ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM <http://ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM>"))
  })
})

shinyApp(ui= ui, server = server)

(http://cran.rstudio.com/web/packages/Cairo/), or the system library

you try to build R from source, which is what I recommended you _not_
to do (try to install the binary package instead). If you want to
build R from source anyway, you have to install the system library
cairo, and _probably_ also pango (http://www.pango.org/). I'm not
familiar with CentOS, so I have no idea about whether you need or how
to install pango.

documentation: http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/ In your
case, I said you could open the JavaScript console, and take a look at
the error message there (in Chrome, Ctrl+Shift+J).

 sidebarLayout(

    selectizeInput('StudiesID', 'Studies 1', state.name <http://state.name>, multiple = TRUE),

  selectizeInput('CasesID', 'Cases 1', choices=NULL , multiple = TRUE),

mainPanel(

  library(cgdsr)

  updateSelectizeInput(session, 'CasesID', choices = Cases[,1])

 output$Cases_values<- renderPrint({

  })

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] embeding a shiny app and change the datasource automatically
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] embeding a shiny app and change the datasource automatically
messages.body_plain:
Hi Prathmesh,

You can embed a shiny application into a page through an iframe, you can see an example of that on the front page of shiny.rstudio.com <http://shiny.rstudio.com>.

For #2, there are a few alternatives to consider:

1. Put your csv file in a location that is accessible from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and have a mechanism on application start to load the file.  (some have put it on dropbox and pulled the data down, others have pulled it from a persistent storage like S3)
2. Redeploy your application on a regular basis with the csv file in it.
3. Open a port to your Mongodb directly and have the shiny application pull the data directly.

Hope this helps
Tareef

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Downloading Saved RData files from Shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Downloading Saved RData files from Shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
Hmm... I don't like hearing about the undecipherable .gz file, but you wouldn't find your data in that zipped file anyway.  What you want to do is have a download handler in the app itself which has access to the RData file that you have there.  HOWEVER, my strong recommendation would be for you to write your survey result data to more permanent storage and access it from there instead.  You could consider solutions like writing it to a central database, a file on S3, a spreadsheet on Google Docs or DropBox.

We are hoping to have an example of how to do that up on our website in the coming week or two if the online resources are not sufficient.

Hi,

Is is possible to use deployApp() with an app created by shinyApp? It isn't working, and I wondered if there might be a workaround.

see below:

 test_app = shinyApp(
    ui = fluidPage(
      numericInput("n", "n", 1),
      plotOutput("plot")
    ),
    server = function(input, output) {
      output$plot <- renderPlot( plot(head(cars, input$n)) )
    }
  )

shinyapps::deployApp( test_app)

Error in shinyapps::deployApp(test_app) :
  appDir must be a single element character vector

Thanks

Tom
